newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares close almost unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares close almost unchanged.

text.p: Israeli shares closed almost unchanged in mixed and active trading on Tuesday unaffected by Wall Street's rally, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.05 percent, or 0.14 points, to 260.39 on an all-share turnover of 137 million shekels against 144 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.17 percent lower at 268.80.

"The market looks good and activity is high. The market made a big move and it can not rise further without fresh news. From time to time the market also needs to decline a little and the fact that it has been trendless for two days is normal," said Baruch Glicksberg at Clal Insurance.

"The market tried to rise today but it was not strong enough. It posted nice gains during the last few weeks and it needs to gain strength before it can rise further," said Elisha Rosenfeld at Lehava Investments.
"Right now there is no economic reason for a further rise but the mood is optimistic and it is believed the market will continue rising," he said.
"The local stock market continues to ignore Wall Street and we saw no reaction to the Dow's rise," Glicksberg added.
The Dow Jones industrial average jumped 143.29 points to 7,214.49 on Monday beating the old record set in March.

The most active shares were Israel Discount Bank which fell 0.75 percent to 357 agorot on turnover of 7.7 million shekels; Discount Investments, which gained 1.75 percent to 26,430 agorot on volume of 6.8 million shekels; and Koor Industries, which fell 0.5 percent to 29,707 agorot on turnover of 6.0 million shekels.
